panels.description: Wide, dawn light through the slats of a thatched stable. A grey horse with a black mane lies on his side in the straw, flanks heaving. Nagoji sits in the straw beside him in his commander's dress (rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots), sleeves pushed up; thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN CHIN, small gold ear stud, long curly black hair under the turban, lean cavalryman build, first grey at the temples. Two grooms hang back at the stable door, keeping their distance.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The horse died on the third day of the fever.

panels.description: Close. Nagoji's LEFT hand flat on the grey neck, the nails healed but ridged; the Portuguese brand on the left forearm where the sleeve is pushed up.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Not as fine as the mount I had lost in the storm, but steady, patient, willing to learn the sand.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had named him Megha, for the monsoon clouds he reminded me of.

panels.description: Tight on the horse's eye, half closed, the lashes still. The edge of Nagoji's hand in frame.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: He did not struggle at the end. He simply stopped, the way a lamp runs out of oil.

panels.description: Wide, late afternoon. The hill behind the estate, a lone tamarind tree. Nagoji alone, breaking hard red earth with a broad-bladed Kerala mammatty (hoe), a long grave opening beside him; turban and sash as in 1.1, first grey at the temples. Far below, the estate roofs.

Sunset. Nagoji standing over a finished mound of red earth, the mammatty leaning against the tamarind trunk, his palms raw and blistered; thick moustache, clean chin, first grey at the temples. A second man's long shadow falls across the mound from off panel.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI (off)
copy.text: He was a good horse.

panels.description: Dhanaji arriving at his shoulder: stockier and a little shorter than Nagoji, short black beard, white turban, indigo-dyed tunic, no sash, talwar at his hip; never a rust-red turban or a red sash. Nagoji (rust-red turban, red sash, clean chin, first grey at the temples) does not look up from the mound.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: He was mine.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: My third horse here, but the best of the three. The first I bought here with my own coin.

panels.description: Nagoji's profile against the red sky, tamarind leaves above him: thick curled moustache, clean chin, first grey at the temple.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: This land is not kind on horses. Not kind on men either.

panels.description: Wide, three-quarter view from the side: the two men on the hilltop against the dusk sky, Nagoji in the rust-red turban on the far side, Dhanaji in the white turban and indigo tunic on the near side. Below them, lamps flicker on a training ground where the evening drill is forming up without Nagoji. Dhanaji's raised hand is silhouetted against the sky as he counts on his fingers.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: How long have we been here?

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: Four monsoons since we washed up on this coast.

panels.description: That training ground by day. A Nair veteran bellowing at a recruit who has spilt his priming powder. Beyond them, on a kalari floor, broad-shouldered youths trading stick strikes, not one of them glancing at the master for approval.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Time after a battle does not move in days. It moves in drills.

panels.description: Close on Nagoji, back on the hill at dusk, looking down at the drill: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud. First grey at his temples: draw it clearly, it is new this chapter.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: You find grey at your temples that you do not remember earning.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: That was how I measured time after Colachel.

panels.description: FLASHBACK. The estate courtyard under a great jackfruit tree. Nagoji lies on a mat in its shade, off the commander sheet: bare-chested, ribs bound tight in cloth, cream dhoti, no turban, long curly hair loose; thick curled moustache, CLEAN-SHAVEN CHIN, small gold ear stud; NO sacred thread, no forehead marks; the Portuguese brand on the LEFT forearm, nails healed but ridged; no grey at the temples yet. His eyes are open on the leaves.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In the first weeks after the battle, before drills ground the days into one long line, my head was full of surf and smoke.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Revathi came twice.

panels.description: Padmini (walking stick, cotton sari hitched, thick black hair coiled at the nape) setting a clay pot of buttermilk by Nagoji's mat as she leaves. Revathi (deep indigo sari with gold, jasmine in her braid, flat-coin necklace, gold armlets, sandalwood line at the hairline, no tali: she is a widow) settling on the low wall near his feet, eyes on the sky.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The first time was on the pretext of grain and widows' stipends.

copy.speaker: PADMINI
copy.text: Do not bleed on my courtyard.

panels.description: Revathi on the low wall, still not looking at him. Dry. Nagoji on his mat beyond her, hair loose, clean chin.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You look worse than the Dutch. At least they had the sense to collapse on sand, not good stone.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Sand is softer. Stone holds the bruise longer.

panels.description: Revathi clicks her tongue and leans in, fingers already at the knot of the bandage on Nagoji's side.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Who wrapped this?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: A Maratha who has tied more saddle girths than ribs.

panels.description: Close on Revathi's quick hands winding the cloth back, tighter and neater. Nagoji's jaw set against the sting of air on raw skin: clean-shaven chin, thick moustache.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: This kingdom keeps trying to turn you into ash.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Do not give it all of you at once.

panels.description: Nagoji on his mat (no turban, hair loose, thick moustache, clean chin, no grey), looking past her, up at the sky she was watching.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I wanted to tell her that part of me had already burnt on that beach, and in the letters I had not yet written north.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I promised your Nagas I would bleed on their earth. I did not promise how much.

panels.description: Revathi ties off the bandage on Nagoji's side and sits back. Level eyes.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Learn to keep a little for yourself.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: And for those who will have to live with whatever is left.

panels.description: Revathi already on her feet, her back to us, turned toward the house and calling; her face is hidden. Nagoji on the mat behind her, watching her go.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Padmini!

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Business returned to her face like a veil.

panels.description: Wide. The estate at midnight, no moon, every lamp out. One figure in a dark shawl crossing the courtyard under the jackfruit tree, carrying no light.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The second time, she came alone.

panels.description: Nagoji awake on his mat in a small room, off the commander sheet: cream dhoti, ribs bound in cloth, a cream shoulder cloth over his shoulders, no turban, long curly hair loose; thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud; no sacred thread; no grey at the temples. Shadows of palm fronds sliding across the ceiling.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My ribs ached. My mind would not stop replaying the moment my cavalry hit the Dutch square.

panels.description: Inset, small and harsh: a fragment of Colachel. Horses driving into a line of blue-coated VOC soldiers through smoke. The collision and the faces. No blood.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The sound. The give. The faces.

panels.description: The door swinging open onto darkness. No knock, no lamp. A shape in the doorway.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: You are not sleeping.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Neither are you.

panels.description: Revathi sits on the edge of Nagoji's mat. Only her profile, her braid pinned up, jasmine pale in the dark; indigo sari, no tali.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Jasmine, and sandalwood, the kind burned at funerals and temples.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Padmini told me you wake screaming. That you call out names she does not recognize.

panels.description: Two faces in near darkness, a hand's width apart: Nagoji (thick moustache, clean chin, hair loose) and Revathi.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Padmini talks too much.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Padmini loves you. That is why she told me.

panels.description: The room from above, two small figures: Nagoji lying on the mat, Revathi sitting at its edge. Through the window, a night bird on a palm frond.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Outside, a night bird called, plaintive and unanswered.

panels.description: Revathi's face, steady, eyes on the dark.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I lost a husband. At the battle of the lagoon, five years before you washed up on this coast.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: He was a fool who charged when he should have waited.

panels.description: Memory panel, washed and colder. A younger Revathi on a fortified wall, looking out over a lagoon's edge where, far off and small, a horse goes down among struggling men. Distance only; nothing of what follows.

copy.speaker: REVATHI (off)
copy.text: I watched from the walls. I saw his horse go down. I saw what they did to him after.

panels.description: Back in the dark room. Revathi's profile, composed. Nagoji's eyes on her.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She had told this story to herself too many times for it to wound her now.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: For a year I did not sleep. I would close my eyes and see his face. Not the living face. The one they left in the mud.

panels.description: Close and low: Revathi's hand reaching across the mat in the dark and finding Nagoji's.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: How did it stop?

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: It did not stop. I learned to carry it. The way you learn to walk with a stone in your shoe. Eventually, you forget you are limping.

panels.description: Their joined hands in the foreground; Revathi's face lifting toward Nagoji.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I did not come here to talk about the dead.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Why did you come?

panels.description: Revathi, close, in what light there is.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Because you are alive. And so am I.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: And I am tired of pretending that is not worth something.

panels.description: Revathi's fingers tracing up Nagoji's arm, past the edge of the rib bandage, toward his bare shoulder where the shoulder cloth has slipped. His hand closing on her wrist.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Revathi...

panels.description: Revathi does not pull away. Nagoji's hand still on her wrist.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: There is a room below the granary. Padmini showed me, years ago. It kept someone alive once, when knives were hunting.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: No one goes there now. No one will hear.

panels.description: Revathi's face, chin up. Defiance, and under it a question. She is giving him the choice. Nagoji's shoulder dark in the foreground.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: If anyone sees you leave...

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I am a widow. I am not a wife. What I do with my nights is my own concern.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (lower, separate box)
copy.text: I did not refuse.

panels.description: Wide. The storeroom in darkness, great clay rice vessels standing taller than a man's waist. Revathi leading Nagoji by the hand between them, both barefoot, moving like thieves. He holds his side.
Inset. A low wooden door in the corner that looks like nothing more than a repair panel. Revathi's hand on it.

A small earth cellar, a single mat on the floor. Revathi striking a flint; a brass lamp catches. The first real light of the night falls on her face: indigo sari, jasmine, flat-coin necklace, no tali. Nagoji behind her in the low doorway.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I have thought about this. Since the night you stood in my hall and told me you were not a man who made promises.

panels.description: Revathi and Nagoji standing close in the small light, both dressed as before.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: I have thought about what it would mean to want someone who might die in any season's campaign.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And?

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: And I decided that I would rather have one night I chose than a lifetime of nights I did not.

panels.description: Revathi reaches up and unpins her hair. It falls past her shoulders, darker than the shadows around them. Nagoji's face, watching her: thick moustache, clean chin.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: We did not speak of love. We did not need to.

panels.description: Bottom strip, full width. The brass lamp in the foreground. On the earth wall behind it, two shadows drawing together into one.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was not the coupling of poems, all moonlight and whispered endearments. It was something rawer.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Two people who had both learned that the world takes without asking, choosing for once to take something for themselves.

panels.description: Lamplight. Revathi and Nagoji lie side by side on the mat, dressed: Revathi in her indigo sari with the pallu drawn over her shoulder, her head on his shoulder, careful of his ribs; Nagoji in his dhoti, rib binding and shoulder cloth, hair loose, clean chin.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Padmini will know.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Padmini knew before I did. Why do you think she showed me this room?

panels.description: Inset in the corner of 9.1: Nagoji laughs, and the ribs catch him mid-laugh. A wince.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That woman sees too much.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: She sees what she needs to see. And she decides what to remember.

panels.description: Revathi sits up, adjusting her sari, and looks down at Nagoji. Serious now.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: This changes nothing. You are still a mercenary with no name and no house. I am still a princess with a dead husband and a living reputation to protect.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: We will not speak of this in daylight.

panels.description: Close on Revathi. A small, private smile, one he has never seen her wear in public.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And the next time?

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: The next time, you will have to earn.

panels.description: Wide. Dawn in thin blades through the cracks of the low door. The brass lamp burned out, one thread of smoke rising from it. The other half of the mat empty. Nagoji alone, sitting up, looking at the door: dhoti, rib binding, shoulder cloth, hair loose, clean chin.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Something had shifted. Not the world. But something in me.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A door I had kept barred since Keshavrao drowned, since my family faded into letters that grew shorter each year.

panels.description: Narrow bottom strip. Close on Nagoji's hand resting on the empty half of the mat, beside the cold brass lamp.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I was still a man with no home. But for the first time since I had washed up on this coast, I was a man who wanted one.

panels.description: Wide. The Adi Kesava Perumal temple at Tiruvattar: a clear river running over black stone, wet moss on the steps, rows of ghee lamps. A small royal party at the river steps, Varma at its head in a plain white cloth. Nagoji among them in his commander's dress but barefoot, his boots left with the horses (rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash; thick moustache, clean chin; no grey at the temples yet).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Varma had ridden here once already, in late May, before the siege tightened, to beg Adi Kesava for success.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: After Colachel, he went again to settle the debt.

panels.description: Inside. Marthanda Varma (V13 face) barefoot, no crown, no crest, no jewels, only a plain white cloth, with a narrow linen dressing on the left shoulder from Colachel, half hidden by the cloth. He lays gold and bundles of pepper before the inner shrine.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A kanikka for a victory he believed had been granted as much by Padmanabha as by powder.

panels.description: The Chief Priest (V13 temple priest face) carrying a long sword out of the sanctum across both palms and laying it in Varma's hands.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The royal blade the deity is said to lend to kings who defend this land.

panels.description: The ride back through green country. Varma on horseback, still in the plain white cloth, no crest, no jewels, the sword laid across his knees as if it were a living thing. Nagoji riding at his side on Kayal, his bay mare with the ochre red-brown coat, watching him (commander dress, clean chin, no grey yet).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had seen him ruthless in war, cunning in council, tender once or twice with a child.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I had never seen him so certain.

panels.description: Narrow strip. The sword's edge catching the sun; the column of riders small behind it.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The work that followed felt like it marched behind that steel.

panels.description: The lower yard at Udayagiri. Former Company soldiers, a mixed crowd of Europeans in torn shirts and breeches, queue at a table of palm-leaf ledgers. In the foreground, Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) counting coin into a sunburnt European palm. Standing beside the table as an officer, apart from the queue: Lannoy (tall, pale hair, long nose, white cotton coat over a white mundu, NOT a blue coat), watching his former soldiers sign on and take coin.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Lannoy chose to stay. Nearly a third of the Dutch prisoners did the same.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Ramayyan had learned it early. A man who is paid feels owned. A man who is owed feels wronged.

panels.description: Large. High angle over a rebuilt fort: bastions thrust out at angles like a jagged star, walls lower and thicker than any Deccan rampart, no safe shadow anywhere at the base. Nagoji a small figure on the lip of one bastion, looking down (rust-red turban, red sash; no grey yet).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Kalkulam was rebuilt on the same star lines and renamed Padmanabhapuram, so the capital would never be without teeth again.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: My stomach did a small, unfamiliar twist.

panels.description: Inset in the corner of 11.2, in dry Deccan colours: a tall, square-cornered fort rising from a crag.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The forts I grew up with were built to impress riders like me. Lannoy's were built to swallow cannon shot.

panels.description: At a half-built parapet. Lannoy (white cotton coat over a white mundu, not a blue coat) crouched, tapping a line in wet clay with a stick. A squat mason with arms like tree trunks squints at the sketch, then at the old square wall.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Make this parapet straight, and a cannonball will punch through. Slope it, and the ball glances off.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: You save stone. You save men.

panels.description: The mason, unconvinced, hand on the old wall. Lannoy already standing, dusting his knees.

copy.speaker: MASON
copy.text: Stone likes to sit square.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: So do men. We will teach them both new habits.

panels.description: Morning. Lannoy (tall, pale hair, white cotton coat over a white mundu, not a blue coat) before a line of bare-chested Nair musketeers in dhotis, loading in unison, a cannon crew beyond. His voice sharp, not loud.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Again. Prime, load, aim, fire. Faster. Together.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: The ball does not care whose fingers poured the powder if the timing is wrong.

panels.description: Afternoon. Nagoji on Megha, the grey with the black mane, before a troop of Travancore horse on sand, the riders wheeling in a loose circle (rust-red turban, red sash, clean chin; no grey yet).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Again. Circle, feint, scatter, reform. Feel the sand.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Sometimes in the same tone, without meaning to.

panels.description: The two of them at the edge of the drill ground, dust behind them: Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean chin, no grey yet) and Lannoy (white coat and mundu). Lannoy tracing rectangles in the dust with the toe of his boot.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Your cavalry should form in deeper blocks. Their weight will punch through any line.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And present a thicker target for cannon.

panels.description: Two-shot. Lannoy insisting, jaw set; Nagoji pointing back at the horsemen (clean chin, no grey yet).

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Shock matters.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: So does survival. These men have fields to return to when the wet season comes. If you burn them all in one summer, who will plant your pepper?

panels.description: Lannoy's glare breaking into a short, sharp laugh. Nagoji beside him. Behind them a knot of soldiers watching, half amused, half wary.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: You are stubborn.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You are surprised?

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: No. You are a horseman. I would worry if you were not.

panels.description: A new bastion on the northern marches, above a narrow pass. Marthanda Varma in court dress (cream and gold, peacock crest, gold necklaces, spear). Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth, palm-leaf bundles and stylus). A step behind them, Lannoy (tall, pale hair, white cotton coat over a white mundu, not a blue coat) and Nagoji (rust-red turban, red sash, clean chin, no grey yet).

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: We will not wait for the Dutch to bring their friends here. We have other enemies in this land.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: The Mysore men. The old chiefs who resent my line. Riders from Madurai, if they decide to come south.

panels.description: Close on Varma. His eyes slide to Nagoji, at the edge of frame.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: This army is not only for white men.

panels.description: The drill ground, days later. Varma arriving with a bundle of blue cloth over his arm, glancing toward the distant sea where Dutch hulls ride at anchor. Nagoji and Lannoy among the officers watching him come.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: If we are to face them, let them see that we can stand in their order as well as our own.

panels.description: Lannoy unfolding short coats of rough blue cloth and stiff felt hats in the Company style. Lannoy himself stays in his white coat and mundu; only the pile is blue. The pile grows. The men around it trade sour looks; Nagoji among them, arms folded (rust-red turban, clean chin).
Nagoji leaning in to Lannoy, low, for his ears only (clean chin, no grey yet).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: We are not Dutch.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I will not dress like a Company clerk in boots.

panels.description: Lannoy (white coat and mundu), unruffled, gesturing at the infantry: bare-chested, dhotis hitched, muskets on their shoulders. Nagoji beside him, unconvinced (rust-red turban, clean chin, no grey yet).

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Cloth does not decide who you serve. These coats make European eyes see an army, not a crowd.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Wear them when the Maharaja asks. Throw them aside when you ride home.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I hated that he was right.

panels.description: Large. Parade day, drums. A long straight line of Nair and Madurai infantry in blue coats and stiff hats, muskets at one angle. Keep dhotis and bare feet below the coats and, above the line, the Travancore banner, a silver conch on red, so they cannot be mistaken for VOC troops. Behind the line, Nagoji on Megha, the grey with the black mane, in a blue Travancore drill coat over his clothes, rust-red turban still on, the collar tight at his throat; clean chin, no grey yet. Marthanda Varma watching from a dais, small in the distance.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a few breaths, from a distance, the line might almost have been one of the neat formations I had once ridden against.

panels.description: The order to fall out. Coats shrugged open, hats pushed back, dhotis loosened, men grinning up at Nagoji in his foreign cloth.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The cloth was only another tool. The men inside it were still ours.

panels.description: Velinadu, a muster field. A mixed unit of Nair and Madurai infantry firing in turn, in their own white mundus, bare-chested, no coats, under the red banner with the silver conch. Revathi (deep indigo sari with gold, jasmine, flat-coin necklace, no tali) stands with Nagoji (rust-red turban, red sash, clean chin, faint first grey at the temples) at a proper public distance, her eyes on the formations and flags, not on him.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Travancore's shape changed under this work. Not everyone liked it.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Your king buys loyalty with guns. It is an expensive currency. When the guns rust, what will hold them?

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Habit. Fear. Pride.

panels.description: Revathi, close, gun smoke drifting behind her.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Habit breaks. Fear changes its object.

copy.speaker: REVATHI
copy.text: Pride is a fire that burns houses as easily as enemy camps.

panels.description: A line of young recruits bringing their muskets to their shoulders in one smooth movement.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She was not wrong. But I could not deny the power of what we were building.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A state that could kill Europeans.

panels.description: Nagoji watching them, his face giving nothing away: thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, faint first grey at the temples.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A state that could, in time, kill men who looked like me, if the map shifted.

panels.description: Inset in the corner of 15.2, a memory in dry Deccan colours: a village near Nashik, black soil, a man walking a field, an old couple with white hair in a doorway.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: In quieter moments I thought of my village near Nashik.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Of Deccan forts that may or may not have heard of a small southern battle called Colachel.

panels.description: Night. Musketeers practising loading drill by lamplight below. Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean chin, faint grey) and Dhanaji (white turban, indigo-dyed tunic, short black beard, stockier) watching from a low wall.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: You could go back. You have earned the right. The king would not stop you.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: And then what? They will either treat me as a curiosity or try to use me against this land.

panels.description: Closer. Dhanaji squinting at him. Nagoji's eyes stay on the lamps (clean chin, faint grey at the temples).

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Either way, I will find myself in another man's web. At least here I know the strands.

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: You speak as if you are resigned.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: I speak as if I have counted. And found fewer deaths in this column than in the others.

panels.description: Narrow bottom strip. Dhanaji laughing, shaking his head (white turban, indigo tunic). Nagoji, the corner of his mouth lifting (rust-red turban, clean chin, faint grey).

copy.speaker: DHANAJI
copy.text: Always counting.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: It is what I know how to do.

panels.description: Wide. Dusk. A bastion above the inlet, the sky the colour of old pewter; far below, Marakkar boats moving on the water like dark insects. Two men alone on the parapet, readable in silhouette: Nagoji's rust-red turban and sash, Lannoy's bare pale head and white coat.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Why did you cross? Before the battle ended. Before you knew we would win.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The question had sat between us for months, unspoken.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You walked away from your own men.

panels.description: Lannoy (tall, pale hair, long nose, white cotton coat over a white mundu, not a blue coat), silent, looking at the water. Hold on him long enough that the silence registers.
Two-shot at the parapet. Lannoy turning to Nagoji; Nagoji shaking his head (clean chin, faint grey). Lannoy's thin smile.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Arras. Do you know it?

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: A Catholic city in Flanders. Yet I served a Protestant company, under officers who thought my faith one step above devil worship.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: They tolerated me because I could build walls and aim cannon. They never trusted me.

panels.description: Nagoji, forearms on the parapet (clean chin, faint grey at the temples). Lannoy beside him, eyes on the water.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: That alone would not make a man desert.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: No. But seventeen years of watching the Company grind men into numbers does.

panels.description: Memory panel: a VOC garrison yard in Ceylon in fever-grey light. Thin soldiers in faded, patched blue Company coats, some bare-headed, chewing biscuit. A whitewashed Dutch colonial fort wall with red-tiled roofs and palms beyond. In a lit doorway, officers in better blue coats and wigs at their wine. No red coats.

copy.speaker: LANNOY (off)
copy.text: The Company paid them late or not at all. The officers drank wine while the soldiers ate weevils.

copy.speaker: LANNOY (off)
copy.text: I wrote reports. No one read them.

panels.description: Lannoy (white coat and mundu, pale hair), face to the sea, picking a chip of stone off the parapet and turning it in his fingers. Nagoji at the edge of frame.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Then they sent me here. To take a beach and wait for reinforcements that were never coming.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: We were a gesture, not an army. A message written in men's lives.

panels.description: The stone arcing out over the dark water, Lannoy's arm still extended. Nagoji beside him, watching it fall.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: I decided I was tired of being a number in someone else's ledger.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: I am forty-three. No wife, no children, no land waiting in Europe.

panels.description: Memory, in the cold grey light of a northern schoolroom: a pale-haired Flemish boy of about ten at a wooden desk, drawing a star-shaped fortress with ruler and compasses. The drawing is all lines and angles, with no people anywhere in it and no writing on the paper.

copy.speaker: LANNOY (off)
copy.text: When I was a boy, I dreamed of building fortresses on foreign shores.

copy.speaker: LANNOY (off)
copy.text: None of us drew the people who would live behind those walls.

panels.description: Two-shot, the last light between them. Lannoy turned to face Nagoji (clean chin, faint grey), one hand opened toward the fort beneath their feet.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Now I build walls for a king who once tried to kill me. But at least I build.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: You are still an entry. Ramayyan has you in his ledgers too.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Yes. But he pays me. On time. In my hand.

panels.description: Memory: a dim Flemish church. An old woman in a dark shawl lighting a candle at a side altar, a rack of small flames before her.

copy.speaker: LANNOY (off)
copy.text: My mother lights candles for a son who is either dead or damned, depending on which story the priests tell that week.

copy.speaker: LANNOY (off)
copy.text: I do not know which pains her less.

panels.description: Two-shot on the parapet in the last light: Lannoy (white coat and mundu) turning back from the water to Nagoji (clean chin, faint grey at the temples), who answers him straight. Leave the lower corner clear for the 18.2 inset.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: Do you ever regret staying?

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: I thought of Goa. Of Keshavrao. Of the first time Marthanda Varma offered me a place.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Regret. No. Question, yes. Often.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: That is something.

panels.description: Inset in the lower corner of 18.1, in cold storm colours: a hand slipping from a straight, taut ship's line, wet and fraying, into black water. The line runs out of frame, with no loop and no knot.

Wide. Udayagiri at dusk, weeks later: the new rampart line, the two men walking it and arguing, Lannoy (white coat) pointing along an angle of wall, Nagoji (rust-red turban) beside him. Beyond the outer ditch, scrub and rock, and in it one tiny muzzle flash.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: A few weeks later, at Udayagiri, someone tried to answer those questions for us.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The flat, hard snap of powder close to hand. Not a practice shot.

panels.description: Tight. A loose strand of Lannoy's pale hair lifting at his ear as something passes. His eyes have not yet understood.
Nagoji dragging Lannoy down behind the lip of the bastion. A spray of stone chips bursting from the parapet near Nagoji's knee.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Down!

panels.description: Below the wall: sentries shouting and scattering, muskets snatched up, dogs barking, a man blowing a whistle, torches running for the ditch. The scrub beyond is already empty.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Somewhere in the gathering dark, feet pounded briefly, then faded.

panels.description: The far bank by torchlight, trampled grass. A Nair sentry's open palm holding three torn twists of cartridge paper, bitten open at one end, with a few grains of black powder. No metal casings, no brass.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: One more mark in the tally of storms we now lived under. Not all of them came from the sea.

panels.description: The guardroom, lamplight. Ramayyan (thin, sharp fine features, receding hair, plain white cloth) with his palm leaves. Lannoy (white coat and mundu) apart, turning the chipped piece of parapet stone in his hands. Nagoji by the door.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: Not our men. Dutch agents, perhaps. Or some Kochi fool who thinks the Company will pat his head.

copy.speaker: RAMAYYAN
copy.text: It pleases me that they aimed badly. It troubles me that they aimed at all.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: They will try again, in other ways.

panels.description: Morning. Marthanda Varma, bare-headed, his hair in a side knot above his left ear, no turban, no crest, eyes flat, addressing two Nair soldiers of his own household: bare-chested, forward-tied Kerala topknots, white mundus, a long Nair sword and a small round shield each, scarred forearms, no priestly marks, no sacred thread. Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean chin, faint grey) and Lannoy (white coat and mundu) stand before him.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: You will walk with Kappittan Lannoy. You will walk with Sawant.

copy.speaker: VARMA
copy.text: Wherever they go, you are their shadow.

panels.description: The two Nair guards (topknots, white mundus, swords and round shields) falling in a few paces behind Nagoji and Lannoy as they leave the hall.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It was protection, yes. It was also a reminder.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: No weapon in this kingdom is left without a hand on its hilt.

panels.description: Wide. Dusk on a wall walk at Udayagiri. Nagoji apart at the parapet (rust-red turban, red sash, clean chin, first grey at the temples); one of the two Nair shadows standing a few paces off, silent (topknot, white mundu, sword and round shield).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: For a little while, another thought gnawed at me.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Revathi had spoken more than once of how dangerous it was to let a foreign officer build teeth into this coast.

panels.description: Closer. Nagoji at the parapet, facing inland toward the dark line of the hills, one hand resting on the stone (clean chin, first grey at the temples).

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: It would not have been hard for someone who shared her hatred of European arrogance to whisper a path to a hired musket.

panels.description: Inset in the corner of 20.2, a memory: Revathi (deep indigo sari with gold, jasmine, flat-coin necklace, no tali) standing in her hall at Velinadu, speaking openly before a room of listeners.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: The idea tasted wrong even as it formed. If she wanted De Lannoy gone, she would say it in a hall where everyone could hear.

panels.description: Nagoji turning his back on the hills, his hand coming off the parapet; behind him the Nair shadow shifts his weight. Clean chin, first grey at the temples.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: She had never been a woman who hid behind bush and ditch.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Love is a poor shield against suspicion. But it is more stubborn than fear.

panels.description: The bastion. A test cannon booms from a lower battery; smoke rolls over the water and birds burst from the trees along it. Lannoy (tall, pale hair, white cotton coat over a white mundu, not a blue coat) beside Nagoji (rust-red turban, clean chin, first grey at the temples); the two Nair shadows a few paces back.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: They will come back. My old masters. They do not like being told no.

copy.speaker: NAGOJI
copy.text: Then we will have walls ready for them.

copy.speaker: LANNOY
copy.text: And guns. And horse. And men who know how to move on sand.

panels.description: Wide, the last light. Nagoji and Lannoy on the southern wall, small against the sky, the two Nair shadows a few paces behind them.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Two foreigners, bound to a king who trusted us enough to let us build his teeth, and distrusted us enough never to look away for long.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Travancore was changing.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: So was I.

panels.description: Bottom strip, full width, low and close: the bare feet, dhotis and shouldered muskets of a new unit moving past in neat order.

copy.speaker: CAPTION
copy.text: Somewhere, in some future battle, a Dutchman or a Portuguese or a Mysorean would stand, baffled, as men from this small kingdom refused to die in the patterns their manuals predicted.

copy.speaker: CAPTION (separate, weighted)
copy.text: That was enough for now.
